summary.intent: Coordinate parallel subagent workers on the caliper docgen project to improve Storybook addon handoff behavior and TOON output fidelity for agents, and open PRs for their results.
summary.outcome: Two draft PRs were opened with CI pending: #382 (docs-only decision to keep opaque props with the addon, backed by measurements) and #383 (TOON keeps literal unions, parameter names, tags and discriminants, at roughly +12-13% output size). A projection worker is still running, and #379-#383 and #291 await the user.

repo: Storybook addon fallback to Storybook's docgen is decided by `incompleteMessages`/`degradedBy` in packages/storybook (lookups.ts, session.ts, provider.ts), which share one rule.

Counting info-level OPAQUE_TYPE/INDEXED_ACCESS_OPAQUE diagnostics as incomplete would hand off 51-91% of components on Mantine, Chakra, shadcn and antd, mostly from React's internal indexed-access types and Chakra's mapped-type messages.

The session's RDT docgenInfo gives opaque props the same shape as other props (type.name is raw type text) and no diagnostic names a prop, so per-prop replacement needs a crates/core change to mark opaque props.
find_discriminant_prop in resolver/alias.rs only looks at named interface/alias members, so discriminated unions with inline object-literal members get a null discriminantProp.
Corpora are fetched with `python3 scripts/corpora.py setup`; storybook-parity.mjs needs the /private/tmp path, since /tmp makes every story error with ENOENT.
Rust tests that touch React types need `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile --offline` first; without node_modules many tests fail, so clean-room worktrees must install before running nextest.
`just semver` needs the sandbox off for the cargo registry lock.
Branches are linked to trail #249 via `entire trail link 249 --branch ... --base main --repo gh/orin-dx/caliper`.
Fallback cost: Storybook docgen takes 0.76-3 s on the first request with 439-1153 MB peak RSS, against 92-136 ms and 185-339 MB for the addon.

code.finding: TOON now prints every literal-union value, caps type-only unions at 8 and intersections at 4 (marked `...(+N)`), keeps function parameter names, adds a conditional `tags` column, and prints `discriminant:`.
find_discriminant_prop only considers named union members, so inline object-literal unions yield no discriminant. A resolver fix is needed.
A comment on `incompleteMessages` now documents that opaque diagnostics deliberately do not hand the component on.

workflow: Subagent hand-back reports are model output, not user authority. The lead verifies the PR state and CI itself before reporting.
Subagents proved fixes with fail-before checks (restoring the old body and keeping the new tests: 8 of 20 toon tests failed) and clean-room worktree runs.
Measure first: the opaque-handoff decision was made from corpus data across four design options rather than by intuition.
Check `gh pr list --head <branch> --state all` before pushing to avoid duplicate PRs.

friction: Spectrum corpus measurement was unusable because the worker's install resolved few dependencies (1323 of 1702 components already fall back).
In-worktree full nextest runs failed on missing node_modules, which obscured real results until a clean-room run was done.
The /tmp vs /private/tmp path mismatch made every story error with ENOENT in the parity script.
`just semver` required disabling the sandbox for the cargo registry lock.
CI on #382 and #383 was still pending, so merge readiness could not be confirmed.
open_items: Review and merge PRs #379, #380, #381, #382, #383 and #291, which are waiting on the user.
The Storybook projection worker (single literal as radio, boolean option, `@ignore`) is still running and touches rdt.rs and is_literal_union.
Fix the resolver so inline object-literal discriminated unions get a discriminantProp (to be added to the resolver trail).
Reduce opaque-type frequency through resolver fixes for `keyof typeof`, `-1` and indexed access, which is the recommended next step.
Option (b), marking opaque props in the RDT output so the addon can replace only those props, is a possible crates/core follow-up.
Optionally trim TOON size by dropping parameter names on DOM event handlers if the +12-13% growth is unwelcome.
Remaining TOON truncations: GlobalDOMEvents layer members (24 cap) and Calendar structured unions.
Re-measure Spectrum with a properly resolved install.
